resolution: When allowed schemas or runtime setup are absent, show the existing specific setup guidance; do not represent missing observations as a healthy zero-error posture.
Refresh remains tied to the current posture and keeps its in-flight state; do not infer completion from dispatch or briefly show a healthy verdict before observations return.
Keep the unavailable source, inspected reason, and existing Search health destination visible; preserve any other known posture evidence.
Lead with the actual trust verdict and its evidence, then preserve the three distinct intent routes for recovery, pre-promotion verification, and search exploration.
Keep known sources and unavailable queue/backend observations separately labeled; never infer overall health from a partial response.

At desktop, intermediate, and narrow widths, wrap full schema/task identifiers and reasons or use existing bounded evidence scrolling; keep controls reachable and avoid document-level horizontal overflow.
Render zero, one, and many configured schemas with truthful counts and grouping; counts alone do not imply search health or successful recovery.
Long schema labels, task identifiers, and diagnostic reasons wrap or reflow with full accessible context; actions retain their text label or accessible name.
No-schema and missing-runtime states retain the exact configuration guidance; do not confuse unavailable configuration with an empty but healthy fleet.
Refresh Search health keeps its label, current selection, and busy state together; do not present old observations as the result of an in-flight refresh.
Show each fetch error with its inspected reason and the existing failed-work route; keep independent schema evidence available.
Show the actual summary verdict and four fleet metrics before the worst-first per-schema signal cards, with Backend and Queue evidence distinct.
An unavailable queue/backend observation remains explicit beside known values; zero errors or a last success does not imply full health.
At desktop, intermediate, and narrow widths, full schema/index identifiers and reasons wrap or use existing bounded scrolling without hiding controls or causing document overflow.
Zero, one, and many schemas retain accurate counts, plural wording, and per-schema grouping; order remains worst-first where applicable.
Long schema/index names and fetch reasons remain fully readable through wrapping or reflow; error context is not hover-only or clipped.
Show “No failed sync jobs” only for an observed empty result, with the existing recovery-confirmation guidance; missing schema/runtime configuration remains a separate setup state.
Keep selected-schema identity, refresh/recovery context, and the in-flight state together; acceptance or dispatch must not imply completed repair.
Identify the selected schema, show the actual failure reason and backend/queue next step, and retain any known failed-job history.
Keep newest evidence first, distinguish retryable rows from retained history, and show Retry accepted separately from authoritative completion.
Keep known failed rows attributable while unavailable observations remain explicit; do not replace retained history with a fabricated complete or empty result.
At desktop, intermediate, and narrow widths, full job/source identifiers and reasons wrap or use existing bounded scrolling; retry controls remain reachable without document overflow.
Zero, one, and many failed jobs use truthful counts and existing row grouping; do not offer retry for an ineligible item or imply all work is recoverable.
Long source/job identifiers and failure reasons wrap with full context; errors and action labels remain available without hover or clipping.
Keep no schemas, no drift, and not-yet-available observations distinct; a missing observation never becomes an empty-success state.
Preserve separate recovery observation, sync/queue refresh, and promotion in-flight identities; refresh observes accepted recovery and never submits work.
Distinguish a failed drift observation from a remote operation failure; retain the actual reason and the documented safe next step for each.
Keep sync/queue evidence, contract drift, freshness, operation outcome, and gated promotion visually and semantically separate.
Keep accepted, running, terminal, unknown, and unavailable observations distinct and attached to the exact task/index identity.
At desktop, intermediate, and narrow widths, full schema/task identifiers, timestamps, and reasons wrap or use existing bounded evidence scrolling without document overflow.
Use truthful zero/one/many grouping for schemas and operations; counts do not imply repair, promotion, or successful reconciliation.
Long identifiers and operation reasons wrap or reflow with the safe next step still visible and the complete accessible context retained.
Keep not-run, successful zero-hit, and unavailable schema/runtime states distinct; a blank query remains a valid exploratory query where the existing contract allows it.
The single Run search action retains dispatched mode, targets, query, and page-size identity with its busy guard; later form edits do not relabel the in-flight request.
Show the actual request/validation reason and the documented correction-and-rerun step; preserve partial per-index outcomes and details.
Attribute returned results to the actual submitted mode, targets, query, and limits; keep the Results region adjacent and explicitly labeled.
Expose each returned, zero-hit, and failed index separately with its reason and next step; a failed index does not erase results or become zero hits.
At desktop, intermediate, and narrow widths, long queries, identifiers, and response values wrap or use existing bounded disclosure scrolling; controls remain reachable without document overflow.
Show accurate target and hit counts; zero hits remains a successful response, and single/multi-index outcomes remain attributed per index.
Long queries, module names, index identifiers, errors, and action labels wrap/reflow with full accessible context; no required reason is clipped or hover-only.
Keep an empty workspace distinct from read-only examples, no selected valid preview, and no run yet; each state retains its own existing import/load guidance.
Import, preview, run, save, and file operations retain the current file/draft/run identity while pending; do not announce persistence or completion before it is authoritative.
Keep actual import, load, save, or run failure attached to the affected file/run with its correction; leave unaffected catalog work reachable.
Keep catalog management, selected preview, run action, outcome, and Search handoff as distinct tasks with source and submitted criteria attributable.
Preserve per-index partial outcomes and workspace/read-only/imported provenance; missing configuration or permissions never becomes invented ready, saved, or complete status.
At desktop, intermediate, and narrow widths, filenames, run identifiers, criteria, and diagnostics wrap or use existing bounded scrolling without document overflow.
Render zero, one, and many files/results with truthful counts and stable row grouping; zero hits is distinct from no run and from failure.
Long filenames, query criteria, run identifiers, and error reasons wrap/reflow with full accessible context; icon-only file actions keep explicit accessible names.
